chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a ram but it perished. He said: 'He should buy another one in its place.' I said, 'Supposing he buys another one in its place, then finds the first one?' He said: 'If both of them were standing (available), so let him slaughter the first one, and let him sell the other one, and if he so desires to, he can slaughter it; and if it was so that he had already slaughtered the other one, so let him slaughter the first one along with it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial ram dies before reaching the place of slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of udhiyah when the sacrificial animal perishes before reaching the slaughter site, establishing the obligation to replace it. It provides a nuanced ruling for scenarios where both animals are present or one is already slaughtered, reflecting the Imams' practical approach to resolving ownership and ritual validity in cases of loss or delay.
